implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 6.1 (Prepare Draft Outputs): LLMs streamline report generation by automating draft outputs (e.g., summaries, tables, charts), allowing analysts to focus on interpretation.
implicated updates.justification: Drafting of all outputs (text, tables, maps) is automated by LLMs/AI, with analysts focusing on higher-level review.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Require that LLMs/AI auto-generate summaries, tables, and narrative reports; staff intervene only for complex, nuanced, or user-facing insights.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Draft outputs—both quantitative and textual—are generated automatically via LLM/AI pipelines, including descriptive statistics, dashboards, and analytic summaries. Analysts only refine, supplement, or tailor outputs for specialized cases, supporting speed and quality by default.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process transforms processed and finalized data into statistical outputs using automated, AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation. Human analysts intervene to interpret, refine, or tailor outputs for specialized, complex, or critical communication needs. AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompany all outputs, documenting analytic approaches and logic. This automation-first approach maximizes efficiency, consistency, and allows analysts to focus on providing added value and insight.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

implicated updates.reference: Key Changes Required - Analyse
implicated updates.quote: Build infrastructure and tooling that enable real-time analytical workflows with intelligent validation and anomaly detection.
implicated updates.justification: Validation must be automated and built into real-time analytic workflows, employing anomaly detection and QA pipelines.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Validation uses AI/ML-powered, real-time digital workflows for QA, anomaly detection, and rule-based checks, escalating only complex or novel outcomes to human analysts for review.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 6.2 Generative AI can help detect anomalies and outliers in data/outputs.
implicated updates.justification: AI/ML and generative models are to be the norm for anomaly/outlier detection in all output validation, improving speed, consistency, and focus for human review.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Automate anomaly, outlier, and pattern detection in validated outputs using AI/ML, with escalation to humans for deep dives or contextual review.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Output validation must be handled digitally and in real time, with anomaly and outlier detection, historical comparison, and rule-based checks fully automated using AI/ML. Human analysts review flagged cases and adjudicate nuanced or context-sensitive issues, maximizing quality and reducing manual validation work.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process is where outputs are validated using automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows. Anomaly detection, benchmarking against historical data, metadata and paradata checks, macro editing, and internal/external confrontations are executed with machine-driven QA and pattern recognition. Complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for review and contextual analysis, ensuring that outputs are validated rapidly, consistently, and with high assurance of quality.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process is where outputs are interpreted in order to understand their meaning and to try to explain them. This can involve viewing the statistics from all perspectives using different tools and media, and carrying out various types of in-depth analysis to gain insight into the results and assess them against initial expectations, based also on an understanding of how those results were produced. Such analyses might include time series analysis and other econometric analyses, etc.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 6.3: LLMs offer insights and suggest explanations for complex statistical results, aiding human experts in making data accessible to non-technical audiences. They also provide visualizations and narrative explanations for better data interpretation.
implicated updates.justification: LLMs/AI are to generate first-draft narrative summaries, visualizations, and key findings, supporting analysts in interpretation and explanation.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Standardize the use of LLMs/AI to generate initial textual and visual analyses; staff validate, deepen, and refine explanation for complex and user-facing cases, driving contextual narrative and knowledge transfer.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: AI and LLM technology should provide automated draft explanations, visualizations, patterns, and interpretations of results, maximizing efficiency and coverage. Human analysts ensure narrative depth, clarity, and context, especially for high-profile or complex explanations.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process interprets and explains outputs using LLM/AI-powered narrative generation, visualization, and automated analytics to provide first-draft explanations and insight. Statisticians and analysts review and refine these drafts, supplementing them with domain expertise, context, and additional analytics as needed to make results accessible and meaningful, especially for nuanced or high-impact topics.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process ensures that the data (and metadata) to be disseminated or internally stored for future use do not breach the appropriate rules on confidentiality according to either organisational policies and rules, or to the process-specific methodology created in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). This may include checks for primary and secondary disclosure, as well as the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking. The degree and method of statistical disclosure control may vary for different types of outputs. For example, the approach used for microdata sets for research purposes will be different to that for published tables or visualisations at the aggregated level. Geospatial data or outputs from geospatial data may raise additional confidentiality challenges in terms of personal data protection and disclosure risk.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Phase — Proposed Change Table
implicated updates.quote: Privacy-enhancing AI tools can automatically apply disclosure control, ensuring sensitive data protection before external sharing
implicated updates.justification: Disclosure control—data suppression, SDC, perturbation—can be AI-powered and automated, with staff reviewing only high-complexity/confidentiality edge cases.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Deploy automated AI/ML-driven tools for privacy/SCD control that stand as the default, auto-applying relevant standards to every output. Manual review is required only when ambiguity or elevated disclosure risk is detected by automation.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 6.4: Privacy-enhancing AI tools can automatically apply disclosure control, ensuring sensitive data protection before external sharing.
implicated updates.justification: Automate disclosure control via privacy-enhancing AI and SCD tools; invoke human review in special circumstances.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Update to embed privacy-by-design automation, with full logging and only high-risk or ambiguous outputs flagged for human sign-off.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Privacy and disclosure control must be automated by privacy/SCD AI solutions, logging all actions for audit and compliance, and flagging only edge cases with elevated disclosure risk for human review. This ensures consistency, scalability, and regulatory assurance.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process applies disclosure control by default using AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools, which automatically assess, suppress, or perturb outputs for confidentiality per established policy. All actions are digitally logged and audited. Outputs only reach human reviewers when the automation detects elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks, ensuring privacy compliance by default and at scale.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process ensures the statistics and associated information are fit for purpose and reach the required quality level and are thus ready for use. It includes: Completing consistency checks; Determining the level of release, and applying caveats; Collating supporting information, including interpretation, commentary, technical notes, briefings, measures of uncertainty and any other necessary metadata; Producing the supporting internal documents; Conducting pre-release discussion with appropriate internal subject matter experts; Translating the statistical outputs in countries with multilingual dissemination; Approving the statistical content for release.

implicated updates.reference: Key priorities of the future state
implicated updates.quote: End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention
implicated updates.justification: All output collation, packaging, metadata checks, and release-readiness assessments should be automated, with staff focused on sign-off and complex or exceptional release decisions.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Update to require automation for all routine checks, collation, evidence-gathering, and documentation for dissemination, reserving human review for final sign-off or issue escalation.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Output collation, final documentation, and readiness assessments should be automated and hands-free by default. Human actions are limited to final QA, release approval, and decision-making for exceptional or high-stakes releases.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process finalises and packages outputs using digital, automation-driven tools and workflows, ensuring all required metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation are produced and collated automatically to the highest standard. Human experts are responsible for sign-off, review of flagged anomalies, and decision-making on exceptional release scenarios or nuanced dissemination requirements. Routine approval, translation, and pre-release briefing are streamlined by digital platforms, maximizing output quality and deployment speed.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This phase manages the release of the statistical data and their products to users. It includes all activities associated with assembling and releasing a range of static and dynamic products via a range of channels. These activities support users to access and use the products released by the statistical organisation. For statistical products produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. Cataloguing and tagging released data and products using relevant metadata standards can greatly increase their discoverability and accessibility both internally and externally. International standards should be used as a norm to ensure that they can be found and consumed easily across a broad range of users. Linking data to geospatial classifications in particular can allow for detailed geographical presentation of outputs. While GSBPM conceives of archiving as taking place within the overarching Data Management and Metadata Management activities, its relevance to finalised outputs in this phase should be noted. The Disseminate phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated updates.reference: Key priorities of the future state
implicated updates.quote:
End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention

- Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination— reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process.
implicated updates.justification: Dissemination is to be fully automated—cataloguing, release, tagging, and product management are handled digitally and in real-time, with outputs prepared in machine-actionable formats and human review for exception and compliance only.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Every dissemination product and channel must be catalogued, tagged, structured, and released via automated and AI-driven platforms, with human involvement reserved for policy guidance, exception handling, and nuanced communication or support needs.

implicated updates.reference: Business Vision: Dissemination
implicated updates.quote:
Expanded Digital Dissemination: Shift focus from static web publishing to dynamic, interactive, and API-driven platforms for more accessible and real-time data engagement.

Automation of Core Processes: Automate production and dissemination of data products (including data tables and PUMFs), improving speed, accuracy, and resource efficiency.

Metadata-First Approach: Implement comprehensive metadata standards and tagging, enabling external tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI agents to accurately discover and extract relevant data.
implicated updates.justification: Dissemination platforms and products must shift to API-first, dynamic, interactive, and automation-enabled models, metadata-rich and ready for digital and AI agent discovery by default.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Dissemination is API-driven and digital-first, outputs published in machine-readable standards with full metadata enrichment, and accessibility and discoverability as core goals.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Phase 7 now requires: (1) full automation and digitization for all dissemination activities (product creation, cataloguing, live release), (2) real-time, dynamic, API-driven and interactive delivery across all channels as standard, (3) comprehensive metadata tagging and enrichment on every released output, maximizing search and AI discoverability, and (4) human activity is focused on policy, exception, and bespoke user service/support.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This phase manages the release of statistical data and their products to users using automation-driven, API-first, and metadata-enriched delivery workflows and platforms. All assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable by both human and AI agents. Outputs are prepared for API-driven consumption, optimized for AI search, and enriched with comprehensive metadata to ensure discovery and reuse across systems. Human staff engage only for policy setting, exception handling, and specialized user support. The Disseminate phase is structured into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which may operate sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as best fits the digital dissemination ecosystem.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.

implicated updates.reference: Business Vision: Dissemination
implicated updates.quote: Metadata-First Approach: Implement comprehensive metadata standards and tagging, enabling external tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI agents to accurately discover and extract relevant data.
implicated updates.justification: Update output systems must enforce auto-loading, metadata-enriched, machine-actionable outputs, ready for API-driven digital release to both human and AI clients.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: All outputs and metadata are automatically formatted, loaded, and linked; systems must enable and enforce API and AI/automation-driven querying, discovery, and downstream use.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Update output systems to enforce auto-formatting, comprehensive metadata linking, and machine-actionable access. Final checks, enrichment, and release must be performed digitally, outputting APIs and formats suitable for automated and AI-driven consumption.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. When the final products raise concern for confidentiality, additional disclosure control may be considered and applied via sub-process 6.4 (Apply disclosure control). Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.

implicated updates.reference: Business Vision: Dissemination
implicated updates.quote: Automation of Core Processes: Automate production and dissemination of data products (including data tables and PUMFs), improving speed, accuracy, and resource efficiency.
implicated updates.justification: All dissemination products should be created and released using digital automation and AI workflows, generating outputs in real-time at scale, ready for multiple channels.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: All data products (tables, graphics, microdata, APIs, etc.) are assembled and published using AI/automation-driven workflows, supporting digital verification and rapid, reproducible publishing.

implicated updates.reference: Key Business Process Table
implicated updates.quote: Make PUMFs mandatory, use automated methods for creation of PUMFs
implicated updates.justification: Producing PUMFs is a compulsory, automated process, with digital workflows and standard formats.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Digital automation must always be used to create, check, and disseminate PUMFs, which are produced as standard outputs whenever possible.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 7.2 (Produce Dissemination Products): LLMs automate the creation of dissemination products, generating draft reports, summaries, or narratives from data tables, which analysts can refine for specific audiences. AI also assists with automated charts and visual representations of data.
implicated updates.justification: LLMs and AI generate dissemination product drafts (incl. text, charts, visualizations), streamlining human refinement and tailoring.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: LLMs and AI tools must be used to draft publications, summaries, graphics, and all product components, for human review and audience tailoring as needed.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Production of dissemination outputs—including data tables, microdata, reports, graphics, and open data—must be automated and AI-driven wherever possible, with PUMFs produced compulsorily. LLMs draft all textual and visualization products, which are then refined, verified, and audience-adapted by human analysts. Production is digital, rapid, and scalable, maximizing quality and speed of release.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process produces dissemination outputs using automated, AI- and LLM-powered workflows to generate, assemble, and format all products—including publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs—as standard. Text, graphics, and narrative products are created with digital automation as first resort, and all products (including mandatory PUMFs) are checked for standards adherence by human specialists, who refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness as required. All dissemination outputs are machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.

implicated updates.reference: Key priorities of the future state
implicated updates.quote: End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention
implicated updates.justification: All release steps, including embargo, scheduled launches, and access management, must run with digital automation by default.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Release scheduling, access provisioning, embargo management, and retraction all take place by orchestrated, automated, and logged digital systems, with staff managing exceptions and policy triggers.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Product release—timing, access, embargo, and audit—is performed digitally, logged, and with minimal manual intervention, allowing staff to oversee compliance, manage exceptions, and support high-level users or critical issues.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. Orchestration platforms schedule, log, and manage real-time releases. Human staff review and approve exception cases, interact with high-level subscribers, and handle policy or retraction scenarios as required, ensuring transparency and compliance at all times.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: Whilst marketing in general can be considered to be part of GAMSO, this sub-process concerns the active promotion of the statistical products produced in a specific statistical business process, to help them reach the widest possible audience. It includes the use of customer relationship management tools, to better target potential users of the products, as well as the use of tools including websites and other platforms like social media to facilitate the process of communicating statistical information to users. These activities may be coordinated with partners in the case of joint products.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 7.4 (Promote Dissemination Products): AI can suggest messaging formats and strategies for various stakeholders, customizing content for platforms like social media, newsletters, and websites to enhance communication effectiveness.
implicated updates.justification: Promotion activities must use AI-driven recommendations and automation to suggest, tailor, and deploy promotional messaging and campaigns across channels.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: AI/automation tools generate, recommend, and tailor messaging for all audience segments and platforms (social, email, web), with staff focusing on review, validation, and optimization of high-impact campaigns or critical communications.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Product promotion and outreach is automated and AI-driven, with messaging, format, and channel recommendations adjusted in real time for reach and effectiveness. Human communicators validate and optimize for major campaigns, critical audiences, or emerging needs.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process promotes statistical products using AI/automation-driven tools to generate, recommend, and deploy messaging across all platforms—web, email, social, and beyond. Content, format, and strategy are tailored with AI for each target audience, adjusting to maximize reach and impact. Staff intervene for high-level campaign review, optimization, and the management of complex or sensitive outreach.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 7.5 (Manage User Support): AI tools like chatbots offer real-time support, helping users navigate datasets, interpret data, and find publications, improving engagement and easing human support workload.
implicated updates.justification: User support is provided by AI chatbots and digital tools for first-level response, with staff escalated only for complex, nuanced, or high-priority cases.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Chatbots and AI interfaces record, triage, and respond to routine user queries; complex requests or unresolved issues are escalated to staff for detailed handling, while user input is used for ongoing service quality improvement.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: AI-driven user support (e.g., chatbots) handle all routine queries, FAQ generation, and first-layer data navigation or interpretation help. Human support is reserved for complex or sensitive cases, or for quality improvement review.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed. Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This phase manages the evaluation of a specific instance of a statistical business process, as opposed to the more general overarching activity of Quality Management described in Section V (Descriptions of overarching activities). It can take place at the end of the instance of the process, but can also be done on an ongoing basis during the statistical production process. It relies on inputs gathered throughout the different phases. It includes evaluating the success of a specific instance of the statistical business process, drawing on a range of quantitative and qualitative inputs, and identifying and prioritising potential improvements. For statistical outputs produced regularly, evaluation should, at least in theory, occur for each iteration, determining whether future iterations should take place, and if so, whether any improvements should be implemented. However, in some cases, particularly for regular and well established statistical business processes, evaluation might not be formally carried out for each iteration. In such cases, this phase can be seen as providing the decision as to whether the next iteration should start from the Specify Needs phase, or from some later phase (often the Collect phase). The Evaluate phase is broken down into three sub-processes (Figure 14), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated updates.reference: Key priorities of the future state
implicated updates.quote:
End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention

- Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination—reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process.
implicated updates.justification: Evaluation must leverage automation and AI for assembling, analyzing, and synthesizing evaluation inputs, prioritizing improvements, and suggesting next-iteration recommendations.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: Evaluation is a digital, AI-driven, and iterative process that continuously aggregates feedback, quality metrics, and performance data from all stages, surfacing actionable improvements with limited manual intervention.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote:
GSBPM 8.1 (Gather evaluation feedback), LLMs can help collect and analyze both internal and external feedback from users, respondents, and stakeholders.

GSBPM 8.2 (Conduct evaluation), LLMs can assist in evaluating the overall performance of statistical processes by analyzing feedback data and suggesting potential improvements for the next iteration of a survey or process.
implicated updates.justification: AI/LLMs are required for collecting, synthesizing, and analyzing feedback and performance data, as well as generating reports and improvement plans.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: All feedback and evaluation data is compiled, clustered, and initially synthesized by AI/LLMs; human evaluators interpret results and approve/modify improvement decisions and forward plans.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: The evaluation phase is now a digital, AI-powered and iterative activity. All feedback, quality metrics, and process analytics are aggregated, synthesized and initially interpreted by AI/LLMs, which also suggest improvements and provide dashboards or summary reports. Human evaluators are responsible for reviewing synthesized results, contextualizing issues, and finalizing actionable improvement plans. This maximizes efficiency, surfaces issues rapidly, and promotes continuous process improvement across all statistical cycles.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This phase manages evaluation for each statistical business process instance using automation and AI/LLM-powered pipelines for gathering, synthesizing, and analyzing all feedback and performance metrics. Iterative, digital-first workflows continuously update and surface actionable insights, with automated reports and dashboards flagging opportunities for adjustment, learning, and quality enhancement. Human analysts focus on contextual review, recommendation adjudication, and final sign-off of improvement plans for future iterations. Evaluation may occur at the end or during any process cycle, and is broken into three sub-processes (Figure 14) which may run simultaneously or be repeated until required standards are met.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: Evaluation material can be produced in any other phase or sub-process. It may take many forms, including feedback from users, process metadata (paradata), system metrics, and staff suggestions. Reports of progress against an action plan agreed during a previous iteration may also form an input to evaluations of subsequent iterations. This sub-process gathers all of these inputs, compiles quality indicators and makes them available for the person or team producing the evaluation. The collection of some of these evaluation materials can be automated and take place in a continuous way throughout the whole process, as defined by the quality framework (see Quality Management in Section V). On the other hand, for the evaluation of certain processes it can be necessary to perform specific activities such as small surveys, (e.g. post-enumeration surveys, re-interview studies, survey on effectiveness of dissemination).

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 8.1 (Gather evaluation feedback), LLMs can help collect and analyze both internal and external feedback from users, respondents, and stakeholders.
implicated updates.justification: Feedback and input data gathering must be orchestrated, digitized, and supported by LLM/AI automation, which aggregates and clusters feedback from multiple sources.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: All feedback, suggestions, and quality metrics are automatically collected and synthesized by LLMs and digital/AI platforms, ensuring completeness, rapid clustering, and continuous readiness for evaluation.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: Evaluation input collection is now automated, AI/LLM-enhanced, and continuous. All formats (feedback, paradata, metrics, staff suggestions) are digitally aggregated and synthesized in real time, ensuring that evaluators always have access to up-to-date, organized, and cluster-summarized data for evaluation exercises.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: Evaluation input gathering is orchestrated via automated, AI/LLM-powered systems that harvest, aggregate, and cluster all feedback, process-metadata, quality metrics, and staff input in real time. Inputs are continuously updated and synthesized for use in ongoing and cyclical evaluation phases, easing the workload on evaluators and ensuring the highest possible input quality and completeness for downstream analysis and decision-making.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process analyses the evaluation inputs, compares them to the expected/target benchmarking results (when available), and synthesises them into an evaluation report or control dashboard. The evaluation can take place at the end of the whole process (ex-post evaluation), for selected activities, during its execution in a continuous way, or throughout the process, thus allowing for quick fixes or continuous improvement. The resulting report should note any quality issues specific to this iteration of the statistical business process as well as highlighting any deviation of performance metrics from expected values, and should make recommendations for changes if appropriate. These recommendations can cover changes to any phase or sub-process for future iterations of the process, or can suggest that the process is not repeated.

implicated updates.reference: GSBPM Roadmap DIGS
implicated updates.quote: GSBPM 8.2 (Conduct evaluation), LLMs can assist in evaluating the overall performance of statistical processes by analyzing feedback data and suggesting potential improvements for the next iteration of a survey or process.
implicated updates.justification: Evaluation is performed by LLM/AI tools, which analyze input data, benchmark against targets, and generate first-draft improvement recommendations and reports for review.
implicated updates.update application to description reason: All evaluation steps—analysis, benchmarking, derivation of improvement actions—are carried out by digital platforms and LLM/AI processes. Analysts review AI-drafted evaluations and improve, reject, or supplement recommendations as needed.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description update reasoning: The evaluation is now undertaken by LLM/AI-driven processes, which analyze synthesized feedback, benchmark outcomes, and draft improvement recommendations and reports/dashboards for human evaluators to review and approve. This speeds up continuous improvement and closes the loop from evaluation to implementation.
Phases and sub-proceeses.updated description: This sub-process analyzes evaluation inputs using LLM/AI-powered digital evaluation algorithms. Automated benchmarking, synthesis, and reporting produce dashboards, quality issues lists, and draft improvement recommendations for each statistical production iteration. Human experts review AI-generated outputs, contextualize findings, and finalize the recommendations and improvement plans to be carried out in current or future cycles.

Phases and sub-proceeses.description: This sub-process brings together the necessary decision-making power to form and agree an action plan based on the evaluation report. It should also include consideration of a mechanism for monitoring the impact of those actions, which may, in turn, provide an input to evaluations of future iterations of the process.

implicated updates.reference: Key priorities of the future state
implicated updates.quote: End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention
implicated updates.justification: Action plan recommendation, drafting, and monitoring adoption are generated by AI/automation, with final contextualization and approval provided by process owners/committees.
